explanation_en: Literally meaning 'to seize' or 'to grab' something by force, this pronominal verb is often used figuratively to mean 'to take up,' 'to address,' or 'to take control of' an issue or case (e.g., 'la justice s'empare de l'affaire'). It is always followed by the preposition 'de', which contracts with definite articles (du, des). When replacing the object with a pronoun, the adverbial pronoun 'en' must be used.

examples.en_text: The thief grabbed her bag before running away.
examples.target_text: Le voleur s'est emparé de son sac avant de s'enfuir en courant.

examples.en_text: An immense sadness took hold of her when she heard the news.
examples.target_text: Une immense tristesse s'est emparée d'elle quand elle a appris la nouvelle.

examples.en_text: The media quickly seized upon this hot topic.
examples.target_text: Les médias se sont rapidement emparés de ce sujet brûlant.

examples.en_text: The army managed to seize the capital after several days of fighting.
examples.target_text: L'armée a réussi à s'emparer de la capitale après plusieurs jours de combat.

examples.en_text: She took charge of the new project with a lot of enthusiasm.
examples.target_text: Elle s'est emparée du nouveau projet avec beaucoup d'enthousiasme.

examples.en_text: Doubt took hold of him just before going on stage.
examples.target_text: Le doute s'est emparé de lui juste avant de monter sur scène.

explanation_en: This phrase means 'to tell the behind-the-scenes story' or 'to share what goes on behind closed doors.' The noun 'coulisses' refers to the wings of a theater, making this a common journalistic metaphor for revealing the hidden details of an event or organization. It is typically used in professional or narrative registers to promise insider information.

examples.en_text: The director likes to talk about the behind-the-scenes of the shoot in his interviews.
examples.target_text: Le réalisateur aime raconter les coulisses du tournage dans ses interviews.

examples.en_text: This political journalist is going to tell us what went on behind the scenes of the election.
examples.target_text: Ce journaliste politique va nous raconter les coulisses de l'élection.

examples.en_text: After the show, the actors agreed to share what went on behind the scenes of the play.
examples.target_text: Après le spectacle, les acteurs ont accepté de raconter les coulisses de la pièce.

examples.en_text: In his new book, the founder tells the behind-the-scenes story of the company's creation.
examples.target_text: Dans son nouveau livre, le fondateur raconte les coulisses de la création de l'entreprise.

examples.en_text: On her YouTube channel, she loves to share the behind-the-scenes of her travels.
examples.target_text: Sur sa chaîne YouTube, elle adore raconter les coulisses de ses voyages.

examples.en_text: If you want, I can tell you what went on behind the scenes of organizing the festival.
examples.target_text: Si tu veux, je peux te raconter les coulisses de l'organisation du festival.

explanation_en: This is a formal, administrative equivalent of 'pouvoir' or 'être capable de,' meaning 'to be in a position to' or 'to be able to' do something. It implies having the necessary resources, authority, or capability to perform the action. It is highly common in professional, legal, and official French and must always be followed by an infinitive verb.

examples.en_text: We are not in a position to accept your request at this time.
examples.target_text: Nous ne sommes pas en mesure d'accepter votre demande pour le moment.

examples.en_text: Would you be in a position to help me with this project next week?
examples.target_text: Serais-tu en mesure de m'aider avec ce projet la semaine prochaine ?

examples.en_text: The technician was not able to repair the machine yesterday.
examples.target_text: Le technicien n'a pas été en mesure de réparer la machine hier.

examples.en_text: Thanks to her savings, she is finally in a position to buy an apartment.
examples.target_text: Grâce à ses économies, elle est enfin en mesure d'acheter un appartement.

examples.en_text: I doubt they are in a position to solve this problem quickly.
examples.target_text: Je doute qu'ils soient en mesure de résoudre ce problème rapidement.

examples.en_text: If we had more time, we would be able to finish the report today.
examples.target_text: Si nous avions plus de temps, nous serions en mesure de finir le rapport aujourd'hui.

explanation_en: This collocation translates to 'a clear youthification' or 'a distinct shift toward a younger demographic' within a group or population. The adjective 'net' here means 'clear,' 'marked,' or 'noticeable' rather than 'clean.' It is primarily used in sociological, demographic, or statistical contexts to describe trends.

examples.en_text: With the arrival of the new interns, we are seeing a marked rejuvenation of the marketing team.
examples.target_text: Avec l'arrivée des nouveaux stagiaires, on constate un net rajeunissement de l'équipe de marketing.

examples.en_text: The latest elections have led to a marked decrease in the average age of the assembly.
examples.target_text: Les dernières élections ont entraîné un net rajeunissement de l'assemblée.

examples.en_text: This classical music festival managed to attract a noticeably younger audience this year.
examples.target_text: Ce festival de musique classique a réussi à attirer un net rajeunissement de son public cette année.

examples.en_text: The change of logo and colors brought a marked rejuvenation to the brand's image.
examples.target_text: Le changement de logo et de couleurs a apporté un net rajeunissement à l'image de la marque.

examples.en_text: Thanks to the construction of the university, this neighborhood is experiencing a marked decrease in the average age of its population.
examples.target_text: Grâce à la construction de l'université, ce quartier connaît un net rajeunissement de sa population.

examples.en_text: The coach decided to trust the young players, which explains the marked rejuvenation of the club.
examples.target_text: L'entraîneur a décidé de faire confiance aux jeunes joueurs, ce qui explique le net rajeunissement du club.

explanation_en: This formal prepositional phrase means 'starting from' or 'as of' a specific date or event. While synonymous with 'à partir de,' it carries a much more administrative, legal, or official tone. It is always followed directly by a noun indicating a point in time (e.g., 'à compter de demain').

examples.en_text: Starting next Monday, our working hours will change.
examples.target_text: À compter de lundi prochain, nos horaires de travail vont changer.

examples.en_text: Public transport fares will increase as of April first.
examples.target_text: Les tarifs des transports en commun vont augmenter à compter du premier avril.

examples.en_text: Your subscription will be active starting from the receipt of your payment.
examples.target_text: Votre abonnement sera actif à compter de la réception de votre paiement.

examples.en_text: Starting today, I am going to try to exercise every morning.
examples.target_text: À compter d'aujourd'hui, je vais essayer de faire du sport tous les matins.

examples.en_text: Registration for the new semester will be open starting tomorrow.
examples.target_text: Les inscriptions pour le nouveau semestre seront ouvertes à compter de demain.

examples.en_text: You have ten days to reply, starting from the date this letter was sent.
examples.target_text: Vous disposez d'un délai de dix jours pour répondre, à compter de la date d'envoi de ce courrier.

idiom: se sentir mal dans sa peau
explanation_en: This common idiom literally translates to 'to feel bad in one's skin' and means to feel insecure, self-conscious, or unhappy with oneself. It is frequently used to describe teenage angst, identity crises, or general low self-esteem. Grammatically, the possessive adjective 'sa' must agree with the subject of the verb (e.g., 'je me sens mal dans ma peau').

examples.en_text: Lately, I've been feeling uncomfortable in my own skin without really knowing why.
examples.target_text: Depuis quelque temps, je me sens mal dans ma peau sans vraiment savoir pourquoi.

examples.en_text: If you feel uncomfortable in your own skin, you should talk to a professional about it.
examples.target_text: Si tu te sens mal dans ta peau, tu devrais en parler à un professionnel.

examples.en_text: During her teenage years, she felt very uncomfortable in her own skin because of her shyness.
examples.target_text: Pendant son adolescence, elle se sentait très mal dans sa peau à cause de sa timidité.

examples.en_text: Many young people feel uncomfortable in their own skin because of social media.
examples.target_text: Beaucoup de jeunes se sentent mal dans leur peau à cause des réseaux sociaux.

examples.en_text: It is difficult to succeed in your projects when you feel uncomfortable in your own skin.
examples.target_text: Il est difficile de réussir ses projets quand on se sent mal dans sa peau.

examples.en_text: After changing jobs, he finally stopped feeling uncomfortable in his own skin.
examples.target_text: Après avoir changé de travail, il a enfin arrêté de se sentir mal dans sa peau.

explanation_en: This transitional phrase translates to 'even more concerning' or 'still more worrying.' It is used at the beginning of a sentence or clause to introduce a new, more serious point, heightening the sense of urgency in an argument or report. In writing, it is typically set off by a comma.

examples.en_text: The drop in grades is a problem, but even more worrying, the students lack motivation.
examples.target_text: La baisse des notes est un problème, mais plus préoccupant encore, les élèves manquent de motivation.

examples.en_text: Unemployment is rising and, even more worrying, many local businesses are closing down.
examples.target_text: Le chômage augmente et, plus préoccupant encore, de nombreuses entreprises locales ferment leurs portes.

examples.en_text: Temperatures are rising every year, and even more worrying, water reserves are rapidly decreasing.
examples.target_text: Les températures augmentent chaque année, et plus préoccupant encore, les réserves d'eau diminuent rapidement.

examples.en_text: Many people sleep poorly, and even more worrying, they never consult a doctor about it.
examples.target_text: Beaucoup de gens dorment mal, et plus préoccupant encore, ils ne consultent jamais de médecin pour cela.

examples.en_text: This software has a few bugs, but even more worrying, it does not protect your personal data well.
examples.target_text: Ce logiciel a quelques bugs, mais plus préoccupant encore, il ne protège pas bien vos données personnelles.

examples.en_text: The mayor canceled the park project and, even more worrying, he refuses to explain his decision to the residents.
examples.target_text: Le maire a annulé le projet de parc et, plus préoccupant encore, il refuse d'expliquer sa décision aux habitants.

explanation_en: This adverbial phrase means 'at first glance' or 'initially.' It is a formal to neutral expression used to describe initial impressions that may later be disproven. Unlike 'à première vue,' which is strictly visual, 'au premier abord' often relates to a person's character or an abstract situation.

examples.en_text: At first glance, he seems a bit cold, but in reality he is very nice.
examples.target_text: Au premier abord, il a l'air un peu froid, mais en réalité il est très sympa.

examples.en_text: This problem seemed difficult at first glance, but we found a solution quickly.
examples.target_text: Ce problème semblait difficile au premier abord, mais nous avons trouvé une solution rapidement.

examples.en_text: At first glance, the city may seem noisy, but it has a lot of charm.
examples.target_text: Au premier abord, la ville peut sembler bruyante, mais elle a beaucoup de charme.

examples.en_text: His project is interesting at first glance, but it still lacks details.
examples.target_text: Son projet est intéressant au premier abord, mais il manque encore de détails.

examples.en_text: At first glance, this book didn't appeal to me at all, and yet I loved it.
examples.target_text: Au premier abord, ce livre ne m'attirait pas du tout, et pourtant je l'ai adoré.

examples.en_text: The job offer seemed perfect at first glance, but the salary was too low.
examples.target_text: L'offre d'emploi paraissait parfaite au premier abord, mais le salaire était trop bas.

explanation_en: This fixed idiomatic expression literally translates to 'shelter and cover,' meaning 'room and board.' It is commonly used in hospitality, volunteering, or informal work arrangements (like woofing). Note that both nouns retain their definite articles ('le') and are rarely modified by other determiners.

examples.en_text: In exchange for a few hours of work on the farm, they offer us room and board.
examples.target_text: En échange de quelques heures de travail à la ferme, ils nous offrent le gîte et le couvert.

examples.en_text: During my studies in Paris, my uncle offered me room and board to help me save money.
examples.target_text: Pendant mes études à Paris, mon oncle m'a proposé le gîte et le couvert pour m'aider à économiser.

examples.en_text: This small mountain inn offers room and board for only fifty euros per night.
examples.target_text: Cette petite auberge de montagne propose le gîte et le couvert pour seulement cinquante euros par nuit.

examples.en_text: Even though I have a job now, my parents continue to provide me with room and board for free.
examples.target_text: Même si j'ai un travail maintenant, mes parents continuent de m'assurer le gîte et le couvert gratuitement.

examples.en_text: The association is looking for volunteers and promises to provide them with room and board during the whole festival.
examples.target_text: L'association recherche des bénévoles et s'engage à leur fournir le gîte et le couvert durant tout le festival.

examples.en_text: When I went to Canada, family friends warmly offered me room and board.
examples.target_text: Quand je suis allé au Canada, des amis de la famille m'ont chaleureusement offert le gîte et le couvert.

explanation_en: This idiom means 'to set foot again' in a place, typically used in negative or reluctant contexts to express fear or refusal to return. It is a neutral-to-informal expression. Grammatically, it requires a preposition like 'dans' or 'à' to introduce the location, or the adverbial pronoun 'y' (e.g., 'je n'y remettrai plus les pieds').

examples.en_text: I will never set foot in this restaurant again, the service was horrible.
examples.target_text: Je ne remettrai plus jamais les pieds dans ce restaurant, le service était horrible.

examples.en_text: After a ten-year absence, they finally set foot again in their hometown.
examples.target_text: Après dix ans d'absence, ils ont enfin remis les pieds dans leur ville natale.

examples.en_text: We promised never to set foot there again.
examples.target_text: Nous avons promis de ne plus jamais y remettre les pieds.

examples.en_text: If I were you, I wouldn't set foot there again after what happened.
examples.target_text: Si j'étais toi, je ne remettrais pas les pieds là-bas après ce qui s'est passé.

examples.en_text: I don't want him to set foot in my house again after our argument.
examples.target_text: Je ne veux plus qu'il remette les pieds chez moi après notre dispute.

examples.en_text: Do you plan on setting foot in this region again one day?
examples.target_text: Est-ce que vous comptez remettre les pieds dans cette région un jour ?

explanation_en: This highly colloquial but extremely common spoken expression means 'it costs,' 'it amounts to,' or 'it will take [a certain amount of time/money].' It is always followed directly by a quantity, duration, or monetary value. Learners should avoid trying to translate it literally, as 'y' and 'en' are fixed pronouns in this idiom.

examples.en_text: Don't worry, it will only take five minutes.
examples.target_text: Ne t'inquiète pas, il y en a pour seulement cinq minutes.

examples.en_text: I bought some fruits and vegetables, it comes to twenty euros.
examples.target_text: J'ai acheté des fruits et des légumes, il y en a pour vingt euros.

examples.en_text: Don't rush, help yourselves, there is enough for everyone.
examples.target_text: Ne vous pressez pas, servez-vous, il y en a pour tout le monde.

examples.en_text: Wait for me there, it will take ten minutes maximum.
examples.target_text: Attends-moi là, il y en aura pour dix minutes maximum.

examples.en_text: We had the car repaired and it cost a lot.
examples.target_text: On a fait réparer la voiture et il y en a eu pour cher.

examples.en_text: With all this washing up to do, it's going to take at least an hour.
examples.target_text: Avec toute cette vaisselle à faire, il y en a pour au moins une heure.

explanation_en: This formal expression means 'as a last resort' or 'as a final option' when all other solutions have failed. It functions adverbially and is placed either at the beginning of a clause or directly after a verb. Note that it does not require an article before 'dernier'.

examples.en_text: We will only call the on-duty doctor as a last resort.
examples.target_text: Nous n'appellerons le médecin de garde qu'en dernier recours.

examples.en_text: She decided to sell her car as a last resort to pay her debts.
examples.target_text: Elle a décidé de vendre sa voiture en dernier recours pour payer ses dettes.

examples.en_text: Canceling our trip should only be considered as a last resort.
examples.target_text: Annuler notre voyage ne doit être envisagé qu'en dernier recours.

examples.en_text: I will ask my parents for money as a last resort.
examples.target_text: Je demanderai de l'argent à mes parents en dernier recours.

examples.en_text: The doctor advised me to only take these sleeping pills as a last resort.
examples.target_text: Le médecin m'a conseillé de ne prendre ces somnifères qu'en dernier recours.

examples.en_text: You should reset your phone only as a last resort.
examples.target_text: Tu devrais réinitialiser ton téléphone uniquement en dernier recours.
